tool: art-department/tools/rig-spritesheet.py --enemy death-beholder (Pillow + numpy one-layer affine rig)
covers: death-beholder.preview.webp (animated flipbook, review only — not shipped)
method: No image model was used and nothing was generated. The shipped painting arrived fully opaque on black, so the black ground connected to the border is first keyed to alpha (graded from its own brightness, so the corona's spray fades out); the enclosed blacks - spines, sockets, mouth - stay opaque. The whole matted painting is then posed as one layer: each of the 24 frames is an affine pose plus a colour grade. The attack is uniform scale only: coil to 0.80 and dim, then swell to 1.14 on the very next frame. Every pixel descends from the existing asset.

tool: art-department/tools/rig-spritesheet.py --enemy green-jelly (Pillow + numpy one-layer affine rig, posed about a foot-line pivot)
covers: green-jelly.preview.webp (animated flipbook, review only — not shipped)
method: No image model was used and nothing was generated. The shipped painting arrived fully opaque on black, so the black ground connected to the border is first keyed to alpha, the same matte as the death-beholder's. The matted jelly is then posed as one layer, and every pose is taken about a pivot on its foot line (330, 548 in source pixels: the middle of the base), not about the canvas centre: it squashes along the floor and stretches upward, wider being shorter. The attack sinks to a squash (1.24 x 0.72), springs off the floor on the very next frame (0.82 x 1.24, lifted 34px) and lands spread wide toward the player. Every pixel descends from the existing asset.

source: gallows-crow.sheet.webp, T's approved image-model sheet (the record above)
method: No pixel was edited by hand. The tool drops each neighbour's sliver by the area centroid of its alpha component, reassembles limbs that crossed a gridline into their own cell, registers every cell by integer translation onto an anchor measured from the idle row (foot-line here), and applies one sheet-wide scale (0.844) so the wing-spread attack fits, then downscales the whole cleaned sheet to 176px cells (A6). method: No pixel was edited by hand. Same chain as the AN5b record, with one deterministic change to the tool made in this phase: a welded core (a quarter or more of its area in a second cell) is now first separated at its neck, by eroding it until it falls apart into two poses in different cells and growing every pixel back to the nearer pose, and only cut at the gridlines when no erosion within a cell/16 rings finds two such poses. The Toll-Keeper's shield bash welded attacking cells 18 and 19 into one core (x 518-1102) through a shield and its smear; cut at the gridline, cell 18 lost the end of its shield to cell 19. The Toll-Keeper's report also counts a second welded core elsewhere on the sheet that erosion never separated into two poses (`welded_split: 1`), the same outcome the Crane-Hook's two thin welds got in AN5b; it is still cut at the gridline, and all 24 shipped cells were checked by eye against it with no clipped pose found. Every earlier set's pixels are unchanged (their reports gain welded_necked: 0). All four anchors measured foot-line. The cave-choir's attack ribbon overshot the 12000 B per-cell ceiling at 176, 168 and 160px (max 14878, 13750, 12758 B), so it is cut at 152px; the other three fit at 176px. The ceiling is not raised. The cleaned sheets are not committed: tests/test_clean_ai_sheet.py regenerates each from its master and checks the sidecar, the report and the pixel hash.
